Outcome:  624 x 201, 16962 x 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE, 2414 x 409 USER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED,
          0 x 5xx, 0 timeouts, ASSERTIONS: PASS
Lines:    20000 — verified equal to the 20000 decisions the server recorded, so this is
          the complete set with nothing lost.

Why this run is local rather than from the deployed service:
  Railway cannot return a log set this size. Two independent caps get in the way.
  1. Ingestion: it drops application logs above ~500/sec per replica and says so inline.
     The deployed 20k runs tripped this (17 notices); even a 4,000-request run at
     305 req/s tripped it 40 times.
  2. Retrieval: 'railway logs --lines' is capped at 5000 ('--lines 10000' is rejected),
     and redirecting the streaming form to a file yields only a 500-line snapshot.
  The deployed logs that Railway will return are in deployed-logs-<date>.txt. For a
  deployment that needs complete logs, the answer is a log drain to an external sink,
  not the platform console.

Format: ECS JSON, one object per line, as written to stdout. Each line carries requestId,
showId, userRef and idemKeyRef. userRef and idemKeyRef are SHA-256 prefixes; the raw
subject and the raw idempotency key are never written, nor are tokens or the admin key.
